quote: We just need to see your Who are you? Who what company are you?
stewart_read: Rep never stated a company name or call reason in the first 30 seconds; the customer had to demand it a minute in.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have assumed the customer already knew Ion from the prior touch and skipped it deliberately to save time.
coaching_implication: Even on recycled leads, state the company name and reason for calling in the opening line — don't rely on the customer remembering a prior rep.

quote: I don't remember who it was. I thought I talked to somebody. But I have some additional questions
stewart_read: Customer explicitly flags unresolved questions and the rep pivots straight to scheduling without asking what they are.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically saving the questions for the specialist to handle live rather than setter-scoping into them.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what were those questions?' even briefly — surfacing them gives the closer a head start and shows the customer they were heard.

quote: Oh, Ion? Okay. Because they called me in regards to a battery one time before.
stewart_read: Second reference to a prior battery conversation that the rep does not probe — what was discussed, why no follow-through.
coaching_implication: A quick 'what did they go over with you then?' would clarify if this is a stalled deal or a dead end, informing the handoff.

quote: Do you mind holding for just a minute? I'm actually gonna go check in with him and see if he has any availability
stewart_read: Strong real-time initiative — rep converts an open-ended 'we'll set up a time' into an active same-day booking attempt.
coaching_implication: This move should be reinforced as a positive pattern — proactively checking specialist availability live raises show-rate odds versus a vague future callback.

quote: It's, like, between, like, four and five.
stewart_read: Rep gives a vague, hedged time window instead of a firm anchor, undermining the button-up.
coaching_implication: State the window firmly: 'I've got you between 4 and 5 today' — drop the 'like, like' softeners that make the commitment sound uncertain.

quote: I'm in the plant, but I'll try to I'm I'm available. I just I gotta make sure I hear I hear him when he calls.
stewart_read: Customer accepts the window but flags a real logistical barrier (being at work) that puts the appointment at risk.
coaching_implication: Should have locked a backup contact method (text confirmation before call) more firmly — rep did offer a text heads-up, which partially addresses this.

quote: I can have him, like, shoot you a text message before just to make sure you're, ready for that call.
stewart_read: Rep offers a low-commitment safeguard (pre-call text) to counter the customer's stated risk of missing the call at work.
coaching_implication: Good recovery move; should be paired with an explicit 'is that fair?' handshake to lock it in, which was missing.
